items.title: Roy Carew Interview, 1964-11-28
items.q: What about, this, Buddy Bowden's blues?

ctx.x: Yeah, and Mr. Jethro. And Anamiel dance?
No, he's got Miserary. Miserary? He's got Miserary and Wine and Boy. I thought he had Mabie done. Miserary, Wine and Boy, Buddy Bowling's Blues, Naked Dance and Mamie's Blues.
Maybe I think about Naked Dance.

items.title: Roy Carew Interview, 1961-06-21
items.q: in as much as the year was 1904, and they've talked so much about Buddy Bolden being on the scene then, I feel that possibly he was one of the players, and his band must have been in the parade.

ctx.x: George K. and I, John Steiner, are interviewing Roy Carew at his home, 818 Quintana Street, Washington, D.C., on June, what's the date? 21st. We've talked briefly before we began about some of Roy's reminiscences, and in order to make this a little more logical to the listener, we'll ask Roy to tell us where and when he was born, something about his family and his earliest

musical inclinations. Well, it's a long time ago. I was born in Michigan, Grand Rapids, and on December the 15th, 1883, and now in my 78th year, my folks came to Michigan from Canada. My father's father, having emigrated from Somersetshire in England to Nova Scotia, then traveled west to Ontario, and my father and the remainder of the family moved over into Michigan in the 1880. I grew up in Grand Rapids when I was 17, and in my 18th year, really, I went to New York for a season, got a job, and earned my living…
The music as well as the words?
